title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: Braised chicken with mushrooms and bacon
excerpt: The long braise is what makes this dish. Chicken legs suit the cooking time far better than breast, going tender and pulling slightly from the bone after an hour in the pot. The sauce reduces to a glossy coat as the collagen from the skin dissolves into it.
sourceNotes: Coq au vin is a French farmhouse dish built on the logic of braising a tough old bird in red wine to tenderise it. Regional versions vary -- Alsatian with Riesling, Burgundian with Pinot Noir -- but the principle of long, slow cooking in liquid holds across all of them.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the braised chicken and sauce for up to 2 months. Defrost overnight and reheat gently.

content.text: Brown the chicken and pancetta in batches and in the right order -- pancetta first for its fat, then the chicken in that fat to pick up colour. Crowding the pan at this stage means steaming, not browning, and the sauce will be pale. Traditional coq au vin uses red wine as the braising liquid; chicken stock gives a lighter but equally satisfying result. A dash of balsamic vinegar can deepen the colour if you prefer.
Fry the pancetta in the saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Season the chicken legs. Brown in the pancetta fat in batches, skin-side down first, for 4-5 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the onion and carrot to the pan and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the chicken stock gradually, stirring to prevent lumps. Add the bay leaves, thyme, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer.

Return the chicken legs and pancetta to the pan. The stock should come about halfway up the chicken. Cover and cook over very low heat for 50-60 minutes until the chicken is tender and pulling from the bone.
Add the mushrooms and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until they are cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Stir in the butter off the heat. Taste and adjust seasoning.

items.cause: Pan not left uncovered long enough after the mushrooms went in.
items.fix: Remove the chicken and simmer the sauce uncovered on medium heat for 10 minutes to reduce.

items.cause: Not browned enough initially, and then covered throughout.
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 15 minutes, or finish the chicken under the grill briefly.
